question: Do MPO/CCM1r/1v labels identify the original medieval book sides, or the present detached fragment/wrapper sides?

bounded_search.result: No authoritative MPO/CCM side-convention definition located in returned results.

excluded_result.reason: Unofficial mirror concerning another manuscript; not authoritative evidence for MPO cataloguing conventions.

bounded_search.limit: This bounded failure does not establish that no official definition exists.

documented_general_method.author: William Duba
documented_general_method.title: Finding the Prior Leaf: Manuscript Fragments and Original Codices
documented_general_method.inspection: Relevant paragraph extracted and complete page visually inspected in newly rendered local preview; no new PDF download.
documented_general_method.paraphrase: Fragment numbers and recto/verso can be assigned according to present in-situ or detached-fragment order. Such naming need not reproduce the original codex reading order.
documented_general_method.applicability_limit: A general explanation of fragment description is not proof of the convention used by MPO, CCM or a particular record.

observed_source_assertions.mpo_fr10370: The pinned record labels k as1r andII as1v.
observed_source_assertions.finnish_iv156_157_173: The indexed institutional descriptions put lowercase opening letters on medieval verso and Roman numerals on recto.
observed_source_assertions.image_observations_in_this_note: No new Fr10370 image adjudication; parent separately reported a k-like mark on image3 andII-like mark on image1.

unresolved_points: Whether MPO r/v denotes medieval book orientation, detached-leaf orientation, wrapper orientation, or another descriptive convention.
Whether convention is uniform across all MPO records and source cataloguing layers.
Whether the particular Fr10370 record transcribes tokens and assigns its descriptive sides correctly.
How intrinsic Latin text succession and both real surfaces establish medieval reading orientation.
conclusion: The difference remains a conditional orientation question. No MPO catalogue error, reversed original leaf or wrong-book identity has been established.
recommended_wording: The MPO side labels and Finnish medieval-side convention give opposite token patterns if interpreted as the same convention; whether that interpretation is valid remains unresolved.
next_evidence: Prefer a specific MPO/CCM cataloguing rule or the actual text succession across both surfaces over assuming provider r/v equals medieval recto/verso.
